To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
zinc-calcium interaction is an important nutritional factor in broiler growth and development.
zinc and calcium interact in the diet and the interaction is influenced by the levels of both minerals in the diet.
the addition of zinc to the diet can reduce the calcium absorption of broilers, and the high calcium level can reduce the zinc content of most of organs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of zinc and calcium on broilers.
the interaction of zinc-calcium on broilers.
the effect of different calcium and zinc levels on growth performance of broilers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the calcium content of 0.75% in diet was the optimum for zinc absorption and utilization of zinc in broilers.

the addition of zinc methionine to the diets of broilers at the level of 50mg/kg is beneficial to the growth and development of broilers, while the addition of calcium to the diets at the level of above 1.25%, especially 1.75%, will have negative effect on the growth of broilers.
high calcium level in broiler diets would reduce the absorption and accumulation of zinc in organs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
high level of zinc and calcium in diets had a negative effect on zinc accumulation in organs and serum activity of AKP.

high level of zinc in diets could improve the accumulation of zinc of pancreas and liver and the activity of AKP in serum, but it had no significant effect on the accumulation of zinc content of tibia.
the high level of calcium decreased the accumulation of zinc and the activity of serum alkaline phosphatase in broilers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
high level of zinc methionine could improve the growth performance of broilers.
the zinc-calcium interaction in broilers is complicated.
the calcium level of 1.0% in the diet is the most beneficial for zinc absorption.
